text:
raj: heads up — ran an end-to-end perf profile on prod-sim tonight. seeing a weird regression in continuous batching when requests include structured output / function calls. p50 token latency up ~12%, p95 up ~28% vs last week's baseline. logs + flamegraph attached in the gist: https://redwood/internal/gists/1951234567

maria: curious — is this the same regression we noticed after the stop-token change?

raj: similar surface but different root. this one spikes when a decode hits a tool-invoke pause (i.e. model emits the function call proto, we pause to run the tool, then resume). profiling shows a lot of kernel-selection churn and KV cache discard/reload around the pause boundary.

li: can you paste the key numbers? even a short table is fine.

raj: sure — from the trace (mixed A100 + M60 tests):
```
baseline (no tool pauses): p50_token = 38ms, p95_token = 112ms
with tool pauses: p50_token = 42.6ms (+12%), p95_token = 143ms (+28%)
batch formation time: median inflight-wait +12ms
kernel-swap overhead events: +75% frequency on pause/resume paths
KV cache miss after resume: ~22% of resumed requests (vs 3% baseline)
```

sam: KV miss that high explains cost — are we flushing KV on pause intentionally?

raj: current behavior: we compact/evict small KV shards when a decode is preempted to free the slot for other batches. that helped throughput historically, but resume-hot-path isn't re-hydrating fast enough, and kernel selection logic sometimes picks the wrong kernel variant when sequence lengths shift after resume.

maria: hmm. two levers: (1) avoid aggressive eviction for requests flagged as "likely-to-resume" (function-call / structured-output), (2) change queue policy to form "pause-tolerant" micro-batches that let those resumes pick up their KV without eviction.

li: do we have a reliable signal to mark a request as likely-to-resume? function-call tokens are pretty deterministic, but structured-output heuristics are fuzzy.

raj: proposal: add a lightweight classifier at enqueue time — if prompt contains function signatures or if client sets prefer_pause_hint header, set request.queue_hint = "resume-heavy". Also treat any message that emits the function proto as resume-heavy for the remainder of the session.

sam: sounds reasonable. what about kernel thrash?

raj: profiling shows kernel thrash mainly when resumed sequences change effective sequence-length buckets (e.g., we picked kernel K1 for short sequences, pause runs other work, then resume with accumulated kv making it fall into K2 path). kernel swap has ~2.5ms penalty on avg because we flush and remap CUDA kernels. I'd like to decrease swapping by relaxing the kernel switch threshold for resumed requests. naive rule: don't switch kernel unless new estimated cost > old_cost * 1.2.

maria: or we could bias the kernel chooser to prefer the currently loaded kernel for the slot for small deltas. combine with a fast fallback check.

li: actionable changes then:
- add queue_hint enum: [default, resume-heavy, no-evict]
- new queue policy "pause-buffer" that forms micro-batches of resume-heavy requests and reserves a tiny KV slab (configurable, default 512KB)
- kernel chooser: implement hysteresis multiplier (1.2) before swapping on resume

raj: implement plan A in a canary (dedicated pool) and run perf-sweep. I'll instrument metrics: kernel_swap_count, kv_rehydrate_time, batch_wait_ms, per-request pause-resume delta.

sam: what token-budget targets are we setting? these resume flows still have short bursts.

maria: set default token_budget_target for resume-heavy = 64 (vs default 32). rationale: slightly larger budgets reduce the number of pauses that interact with batch formation while keeping tail latency acceptable. we can tune after canary.

li: quick note on stop-token scanning — currently we check stop tokens every decoded token which is expensive for structured-output tokens that are often multi-byte sequences. Could we do a batched stop-scan for the last N tokens only on resume?

raj: good call — change: for resume-heavy, maintain a compact rolling hash of the partial output and only run the full stop-scan on new appended segments or when the model emits function-call marker. That should remove a per-token cost.

ci-bot: Test matrix queued: perf/canary/resume-heavy (A100x4), perf/canary/resume-heavy (M60x8) — assigned to li — ETA 24h

li: picking it up. I'll run with --token-budget=64 --queue-policy=pause-buffer and capture the same metrics. will also snapshot kernel_swap_count before/after.

maria: okay, if canary shows improved p95 and KV rehydrate <10% we ship to dedicated pools and then to hosted on a ramp. Also add a metric alert if kv_rehydrate_rate > 15% post-deploy.

raj: I'll open the PR for queue_hint + kernel hysteresis today. li — can you run the perf jobs and drop the traces in the gist? Sam will own stop-scan change PR.

sam: ack — will prototype stop-hash approach in a small branch.

li: starting perf run now. ETA ~3h for first pass.

maria: thanks team. small follow-up: add a note in the runtime docs about queue_hint and expected semantics (specifically that clients can opt-in with prefer_pause_hint). we should keep client opt-in so we don't change baseline behavior unknowingly.

raj: agreed. also adding a short experiment where we disable eviction only for the first 2s after a pause-resume to see if short grace reduces rehydrate churn.

ci-bot: perf run completed for A100x4 (id: prf-1951234567-a100). artifacts: https://redwood/internal/perf/prf-1951234567-a100 — p95_token improved to 118ms (was 143ms). KV_rehydrate_rate down to 9%.

li: initial numbers look promising. posting flamegraphs now.

maria: great — let's keep the canary running for 24h and sync tomorrow with a short summary. :thumbsup:
